# Positive-part and top-three profiles in the exact residual dual

This note combines the audited finite residual-program dual with the
audited distal-truncation inequality. It retains actual global cap labels
and all local positive-part surpluses. It proves identities and cap-load
bounds, not a numerical bound on those loads by the parity budget.

## 1. Actual local profiles, including degenerate cap traces

Let a finite family of closed ambient caps H_1,...,H_N cover the mixed
set's positive q-dimensional fibers, q>=1. At base p_i write

    A_(a,i)=H_q(K_(p_i) intersect H_a),    V_i=H_q(K_(p_i)).

For every alpha>=0, the distal-truncation theorem
`candidate cd833c78fb705a2e` gives

    E_i(alpha):=sum_a(A_(a,i)-alpha)_+ +alpha/gamma_q-V_i >=0,
    gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q.                                (1)

For clarity, it applies intrinsically and includes restrictions which
are constant on a fiber. An empty cap trace contributes zero. If a cap
contains the whole fiber, its single term together with alpha/gamma_q
already proves (1): for alpha<=V_i this is
V_i-alpha+alpha/gamma_q>=V_i, and for alpha>=V_i it is immediate.

Otherwise all positive traces are proper intrinsic halfspaces. For each
A_(a,i)>alpha remove a distal portion of its trace of volume
A_(a,i)-alpha, by a parallel threshold. Such a threshold exists by
continuity of the volume cut by a nonzero intrinsic normal. Intersecting
the remaining halfspaces with the fiber leaves a compact convex remainder
of volume at least V_i-sum_a(A_(a,i)-alpha)_+. Every original cap has
remaining volume at most alpha and the original caps still cover that
remainder. If it has positive volume, its centroid and ordinary intrinsic
Grünbaum give remaining volume at most alpha/gamma_q; if it has zero
volume the desired inequality is already immediate. Proper boundaries
have zero q-measure. This rederives (1) and does not discard a whole-fiber
boundary trace.

Order the actual local cap areas as A_(1)(i)>=A_(2)(i)>=A_(3)(i)>=...,
choosing any fixed ordering of ties. Missing positions when N<3 have
value zero and no original cap label. Put

    kappa_q=1/gamma_q-2>=0.

For q=1 this is zero. Taking alpha=A_(3)(i) in (1) gives

    E_i^top:=A_(1)(i)+A_(2)(i)+kappa_q A_(3)(i)-V_i>=0.  (2)

The identity holds also at ties and at zero third area: only entries
strictly above the third area contribute to the positive parts, and their
sum is A_(1)+A_(2)-2A_(3).

## 2. General weighted positive-part accounting at dual contacts

Use the KKT contact weights rho_i from
`candidate 99d50c87eb055f05`,
and put

    T=sum_i rho_i V_i.

The underlying residual program can use any t>=1 in this section. For
arbitrary chosen local thresholds alpha_i>=0, multiply the exact definition
in (1) by rho_i and sum. This gives

    T+sum_i rho_i E_i(alpha_i)
      =sum_a sum_i rho_i(A_(a,i)-alpha_i)_+
         +(1/gamma_q)sum_i rho_i alpha_i.                (3)

For each cap a define its explicit threshold load

    L_a(alpha)=max{rho_i: A_(a,i)>alpha_i},

with zero maximum for an empty set. Then

    sum_i rho_i(A_(a,i)-alpha_i)_+
       <=L_a(alpha) mu(H_a),                            (4)

because only contact bases above the threshold contribute, each coefficient
is at most the displayed maximum, and their captured volumes are part of
the original global cap mass. Consequently, if mu(H_a)<=B for every a,

    T+sum_i rho_i E_i(alpha_i)
       <=B sum_a L_a(alpha)
          +(1/gamma_q)sum_i rho_i alpha_i.               (5)

No equality or uniformity of local areas was assumed. In particular the
surplus term on the left is not dropped by an unsupported sign claim on
cross-fiber dispersion. The exact expression (3) may be preferable to the
coarser maximum-load bound (4) when actual fiber masses are available.

## 3. The t=1 residual identity and top-three loads

Now specialize the residual program to t=1. Then

    e_i^q=V_i-A_(1)(i),
    R=sum_i rho_i e_i^q,
    T-R=sum_i rho_i A_(1)(i).                            (6)

The first identity follows directly from taking the best single original
cap; the second is the exact KKT identity, including its separate q=1
zero-residual convention.

Let a_s(i) be the original cap label in rank s=1,2,3, omitting missing
positions. Equation (2), together with (6), gives the exact formula

    R+sum_i rho_i E_i^top
       =sum_i rho_i[A_(2)(i)+kappa_q A_(3)(i)].           (7)

Define per-original-cap coefficients

    D_a^23=max_i rho_i[1_{a=a_2(i)}+kappa_q 1_{a=a_3(i)}],
    D_a^123=max_i rho_i[1_{a=a_1(i)}+1_{a=a_2(i)}
                                      +kappa_q 1_{a=a_3(i)}].

Each cap occupies at most one rank at a given base. Expanding the right
side of (7) by original cap labels and bounding each coefficient by its
maximum proves

    R+sum_i rho_i E_i^top <= sum_a D_a^23 mu(H_a),         (8)
    T+sum_i rho_i E_i^top <= sum_a D_a^123 mu(H_a).        (9)

In particular

    B sum_a D_a^123 >= T+sum_i rho_i E_i^top.             (10)

This is a direct interface between the exact convex-residual dual and
actual per-fiber top-three cap profiles. The normalizing measure in T is
the KKT contact measure, not silently the original fiber measure. Ties may
be ordered to minimize a load expression; there are finitely many choices,
so such a minimum is attained. No benefit from an unchosen tie ordering is
assumed.

If a stronger hereditary continuous constant is proved for a specified
local cap class, the same derivation replaces gamma_q throughout by that
constant, provided the distal-trimming hypothesis really remains valid
for the restricted measures. It is not enough to know a constant only for
one untrimmed body. No such extension is assumed in (1)--(10).

## 4. Sharp product calibration and unresolved arithmetic step

For k isolated equal planar simplex fibers with canonical centroid caps,
the t=1 residual roots are all (5V/9)^(1/2). The optimal convex threshold
is constant on the base. A valid optimal dual is the diagonal coupling,
with rho_i=1 at every fiber. Thus T=kV=M and R=5M/9. Each fiber's three
own caps have area4V/9 and E_i^top=0. Their rank coefficients are
1,1,1/4, so sum_a D_a^123=(9/4)k. Equation (10) then gives exactly

    B>=M/[(9/4)k]=(4/9)M/k.

This illustrates the exact constants without asserting that every family
has this diagonal dual or these loads. In general the martingale dual can
concentrate contact weights at a few bases and send mass to noncontact
destinations. Neither T<=M nor sum_a D_a^123<=(9/4)k follows from KKT.
An additional proved arithmetic or geometric estimate is required to turn
(10) into the full OC bound.
